summary: On Shabbos our animals must rest, so they may not carry loads into the street. But they may wear things that guard them or help lead them, like a halter or a chain.
stIntro: Due to the mitzva to rest one’s animals on Shabbat, one’s animal may not go out into the public domain bearing a burden. However, an object designated to protect the animal or to prevent it from fleeing is not considered a burden; therefore, an animal bearing objects that serve that purpose may go out into the public domain. The mishna asks:

chunks.he: בַּמֶּה בְּהֵמָה יוֹצְאָה וּבַמָּה אֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה.
chunks.en: With what may an animal go out on Shabbos, and with what may it not go out?
chunks.st: With what may an animal go out into the public domain on Shabbat and with what may it not go out?

chunks.en: A camel may go out with a halter,
chunks.st: A camel may go out on Shabbat with an afsar,

chunks.en: and a female camel with a nose ring,
chunks.st: and a naka may go out with a ḥatam,
chunks.basisNote: The explanations of these words follow Bartenura.

words.note: A special white camel that needs extra guarding.

chunks.en: and a Libyan donkey with a strong bridle,
chunks.st: and a luvdekim may go out with a perumbiya.
chunks.stMore: All these terms will be defined in the Gemara.
chunks.basisNote: The explanations of these words follow Bartenura.

chunks.en: and a horse with a neck chain.
chunks.st: And a horse may go out with a chain around its neck.

chunks.en: And all animals that wear a chain may go out
chunks.st: And, in general, all animals that typically have a chain around their necks when they go out to the public domain may go out

chunks.en: with the chain and be pulled by the chain.
chunks.st: with a chain on Shabbat and may be pulled by the chain. If these chains contracted ritual impurity,

chunks.en: And if the chains become tamei, we may sprinkle on them and dip them in a mikvah right where they are.
chunks.explain: We do not need to take them off the animal first.
chunks.st: one may sprinkle waters of purification on them and immerse them in their place
chunks.stMore: on the animal, and they need not first be removed.

summary: This mishnah lists more things animals may wear on Shabbos, like a donkey's blanket or a cloth on a lamb. Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Yehudah limit some of them.

chunks.en: A donkey may go out with a blanket
chunks.st: A donkey may go out on Shabbat with a saddlecloth that protects it from the cold

chunks.en: when it is tied onto it.
chunks.st: when it is tied to
chunks.stMore: the animal, and there is no room for concern lest it fall.

chunks.en: Rams may go out with a leather covering tied on.
chunks.st: Rams may go out levuvin.
chunks.basisNote: The meaning of this word follows Bartenura.

chunks.en: Ewes may go out with their tails tied up,
chunks.st: Ewes may go out sheḥuzot,
chunks.basisNote: The meanings of these words follow Bartenura.

chunks.en: or tied down, or wrapped in a cloth.
chunks.explain: The cloth keeps a young lamb's wool clean.
chunks.st: kevulot, and kevunot.
chunks.stMore: All of these terms are discussed and explained in the Gemara.
chunks.basisNote: The meanings of these words follow Bartenura.

chunks.en: Goats may go out with their udders tied.
chunks.st: She-goats may go out with their udders bound.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei forbids all of them,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei prohibits the animals from going out with all of these items, as he considers them burdens,

chunks.en: except for the wrapped ewes.
chunks.st: except for the ewes that are kevunot.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: goats may go out tied to dry up their milk,
chunks.st: Goats may go out on Shabbat with their udders bound to dry
chunks.stMore: their milk supply and discontinue their lactation, in order to facilitate conception. In that case, they are tied with a tight, permanent knot, and there is no concern lest it fall in the public domain.

chunks.en: but not to save the milk.
chunks.explain: Then it is tied loosely and may fall off.
chunks.st: However, they may not go out with their udders bound to conserve their milk, as in that case they are bound loosely.

summary: Some things an animal may not wear on Shabbos, like a rag hanging from it or ropes tying its legs. We also may not tie camels together and pull them as a line.

chunks.en: And with what may it not go out?
chunks.st: And with what may an animal not go out into the public domain on Shabbat?

chunks.en: A camel may not go out with a hanging cloth,
chunks.st: A camel may not go out with a saddlecloth,

chunks.en: not with its legs tied this way or that way,
chunks.explain: These were ways of tying legs so the camel could not run away.
chunks.st: nor may it go out akud or ragul,
chunks.stMore: which are different ways of tying its legs together, as will be explained in the Gemara.

chunks.en: and the same for all other animals.
chunks.st: And likewise, tying all other animals in those manners is prohibited. And likewise,

chunks.he: לֹא יִקְשֹׁר גְּמַלִּים זֶה בָזֶה וְיִמְשֹׁךְ.
chunks.en: One may not tie camels to each other and pull them.
chunks.st: one may not tie camels one to the other and pull
chunks.stMore: the lead camel, thereby pulling the others after it.

chunks.he: אֲבָל מַכְנִיס חֲבָלִים לְתוֹךְ יָדוֹ וְיִמְשֹׁךְ,
chunks.en: But he may take the ropes in his hand and pull,
chunks.st: However, he may place the ropes tied to each of the camels in his hand and pull them all,

chunks.en: as long as he does not twist them together.
chunks.st: provided that he does not intertwine the ropes.

summary: This mishnah lists more things animals may not go out with on Shabbos, like a bell or a strap. Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah's cow went out with a strap between its horns, but the Sages did not agree.
stIntro: This mishna lists additional objects with which an animal may not go out into the public domain on Shabbat:

chunks.en: A donkey may not go out with a blanket
chunks.st: A donkey may neither go out with the saddlecloth

chunks.en: when it is not tied onto it,
chunks.st: when it is not tied to its back,

chunks.en: and not with a bell,
chunks.st: nor with a bell

chunks.en: even though it is stopped up,
chunks.st: even if it is plugged to prevent it from ringing,

chunks.en: and not with a ladder on its neck,
chunks.explain: Wooden bars on its neck kept it from scratching a sore.
chunks.st: nor with a ladder that is around its neck,

chunks.en: and not with a strap on its leg.
chunks.st: nor with a strap that is around its leg.

chunks.en: Roosters may not go out with strings,
chunks.st: And the roosters may not go out with strings

chunks.en: and not with straps on their feet.
chunks.st: and not with a strap on their feet, which are tied there as a sign of ownership.

chunks.en: Rams may not go out with a little wagon
chunks.st: And the rams may not go out with a small wagon

chunks.en: under their tails.
chunks.explain: It kept a long tail from dragging on the ground.
chunks.st: under their tails,
chunks.stMore: as it was common practice to put a small wagon under the tails of grown sheep so that the tail would not be injured by dragging on the ground.

chunks.en: Ewes may not go out with a twig in their nose.
chunks.st: And ewes may not go out ḥanunot,
chunks.basisNote: The meaning of this word follows Bartenura.

chunks.en: A calf may not go out with a small yoke,
chunks.st: nor may a calf go out with a gimon,

chunks.en: and not a cow with a hedgehog skin,
chunks.st: nor may a cow go out with the skin of a hedgehog [kupar],

chunks.en: and not with a strap between its horns.
chunks.st: nor with a strap between its horns. The mishna relates that

chunks.he: פָּרָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
chunks.en: The cow of Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya’s cow

chunks.en: used to go out with a strap between its horns,
chunks.st: would go out on Shabbat with a strap between its horns,

chunks.en: but the Sages did not agree.
chunks.st: contrary to the will of the Sages.
